how: One source mutation in the working tree, the named suite run against it, then the file restored from a byte-identical copy and `git status` re-checked empty before the next row (X14/X15/G8/G15's convention: `before` is the shipped source the row ran against, `after` the text that replaced it). JVM rows are `example/android $ ./gradlew :react-native-nitro-ui:testDebugUnitTest --tests <class>`, off-device. Device rows ran on lease E3-o7x7a (pair-b: emulator-5570, iPhone 17 simulator, Metro 8293) through `node scripts/gate.mjs`, and every one of them is a *filtered* run (`harness:android:Menu`, `real-input:android:--control:menu`), so it satisfies nothing but its own name; the code tree is in each row because it moves with every mutation. Rows marked `organic` are not mutations: they are a new test going red against the shipped component before the test itself was fixed, which is the stronger evidence. Rows marked `negative control` are mutations that were expected to go red and did not; they are kept because each one is the reason a claim in a comment or a doc says what it now says.

mutations.run: harness:android:Menu — FAIL, 1 failed of 48 (code tree e955bdb1b9f9, lease E3-5z5a2; the other 47 passed, ContextMenu's 22 with them)
redTests: earns its own box, which is not the plain trigger's — `testID "split-size" (split-size) never reached 124.95x48.00 - last box 78.86x48.00, control measured 124.95x48.00` (Menu.harness.tsx:401)
mutations.finding: The claim the review doubted holds. The harness poisons keys it computes itself, and this mutation still sends the *plain* key, which is poisoned - and shared. A correction to a shared entry is the answer every holder of it gets, so the split control is laid out at the plain trigger's width and the case goes red on the control that measured first. `corrections >= 2` does still hold on its own, which is why the assertion that catches it is the box, not the count.
